name: Pebblely
tagline: Generate product-photo backgrounds from uploaded cutouts and reusable prompts

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; a trial may be offered, but there is no permanent free allowance on the pricing page
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; yearly is advertised as more than 2 months free, but exact annual-effective USD amounts were not exposed
pricing.hiddenCosts: Subscriptions auto-renew. The official page does not state that unused monthly image allowances roll over.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Pebblely, generate product-photo backgrounds from uploaded cutouts and reusable prompts. The hard boundary is specialized model tuning, fast cloud generation, and commerce workflow, plus frontier models, compute, and data.
coreLoopDIY: Generate product-photo backgrounds from uploaded cutouts and reusable prompts, submit jobs to a user-owned model server, and keep outputs reproducible.
requirements: GPU-capable machine or user-supplied generation API
whatYouLose: specialized model tuning, fast cloud generation, and commerce workflow
replacementScope: local workflow manager, not a model replacement
ongoingBurden: GPU procurement, model licensing, safety filters, queueing, storage, and rapid model replacement
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Pebblely because the product value is the model and compute fleet, not the prompt box around it. The recurring cost buys GPU procurement, model licensing, safety filters, queueing, storage, and rapid model replacement, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: ComfyUI
priorArt.desc: Node-based open-source diffusion workflow engine with a large ecosystem.

alternatives.name: Krita AI Diffusion
alternatives.desc: Mask the cutout and generate reusable product backgrounds in layers; slower, but not credit-shaped.

alternatives.name: NodeTool
alternatives.desc: Remove the background, keep the product, generate the scene and save the workflow for the next SKU.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a local workflow manager, not a model replacement DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Pebblely in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, ComfyUI as a local worker, and a small React frontend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: generate product-photo backgrounds from uploaded cutouts and reusable prompts, submit jobs to a user-owned model server, and keep outputs reproducible.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create prompt, negative-prompt, seed, dimensions, model, and workflow controls.
Submit jobs only to the local ComfyUI endpoint configured in .env.
Record exact generation parameters and workflow JSON beside every output.
Build a searchable contact sheet with compare, favorite, annotate, and rerun actions.
Support local image-to-image and mask inputs without uploading them elsewhere.
Show estimated VRAM needs and fail clearly when a workflow or model is missing.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out training a new frontier model.
Deliberately leave out copying a vendor's proprietary model or dataset.
Deliberately leave out public generation hosting and moderation.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
